candidates.text: According to the Kegan stages of adult development: if your anger is subject, that means you can’t be self-aware about it (it has control of you, driving you without your conscious awareness), so you act impulsively (hitting walls, scaring your family, causing damage). When your anger is object, you *can* see and be self-aware about it, which means you can take precautions - creating a safe environment for yourself to release aggression (away from your family, without breaking anything). In the end, the visible anger and act of aggression look similar, but the difference in mental state is important because in one instance the person is in control of themselves and in the other they’re not

candidates.text:
Am I the only one who doesn’t understand why we need data centers?

I spent all morning searching Google and Wikipedia and couldn’t find a single good reason. Then I watched a 45-minute YouTube explainer in 4K, but it was mostly about AI, and I’m just waiting for that bubble to pop.

I opened 200 browser tabs, downloaded a few hundred research papers, translated three from Chinese, and uploaded 2TB of sequencing data so colleagues in eight countries could analyze it with me. Then we discussed the results on Zoom while Slack transcribed the meeting and emailed everyone a summary.

Around lunch, my phone backed up 14,000 family photos, synchronized my contacts and calendar across six devices, routed me around traffic, checked the weather using live satellite data, booked a doctor’s appointment, refilled a prescription, paid a bill, transferred money between banks, approved payroll for hundreds of employees, and ordered groceries.

Later, I read about hospitals retrieving patient records and medical scans in seconds, emergency services coordinating disaster responses, scientists designing protein therapies and sharing enormous datasets, utilities balancing the electrical grid, and airlines continuously rerouting thousands of flights.

But these all felt like pretty niche edge cases.

So I asked an AI agent to turn everything I had done that day into a Twitter post, make it increasingly insane and obvious, and optimize it for maximum engagement.

candidates.text:
The fact that ITC started diversifying away from its main tobacco business into hotels and other businesses after almost 70 years of existence was an immense feat of foresight. Especially considering ITC was never a founder-driven company.

They knew tobacco was extremely harmful to health and addictive. When something is bad for people but difficult to ban outright, governments invariably keep regulating and taxing it more. Over time, the taxes become so high and the revenues so significant that the government itself ends up in a strange place: ban it or continue taxing it?

I can’t help but see a parallel with the broking industry.😬

F&O trading is bad for almost 99% of retail traders. It is unlikely to be banned outright, but regulation will probably keep getting tighter, and taxes like STT will probably keep going higher.

Running a business in an industry with constant government scrutiny over consumer protection is not easy, to say the least. The risk isn’t just economic, but that regulators can ban entire business models almost overnight.

So yeah, the only thing we can do is keep diversifying our business while the core business is still doing well.

Was listening to Intermission by @TheKenWeb, an episode on ITC, and this thought stuck with me.
